files.reasons.unavailable: The machine holding these files cannot be reached right now.
files.reasons.read_only: This tree is read-only for you.
files.reasons.one_at_a_time: This works on one entry at a time.
files.reasons.folder_nothing_to_edit: A folder has nothing to edit. Open it instead.
files.reasons.symlink_edit: This is a link. The panel reports links and never follows them, so open what it points at directly.
files.reasons.file_too_large_to_open: This file is larger than the panel will open. Download it instead.
files.reasons.folder_cannot_download: A folder cannot be downloaded as it is. Compress it first, then take the archive.
files.reasons.symlink_download: This is a link, and following it could leave this tree. Download what it points at instead.
files.reasons.not_an_archive: That is not an archive this panel can unpack.
files.reasons.measure_one: This measures one folder at a time.
files.reasons.file_shows_size: A file already shows its size in the list.
files.page.title: Files
files.page.page_desc: {root}, on the machine holding {service}. There is no SFTP: this is the way in.
files.page.upload_refusal_unavailable: Uploading is off while this tree cannot be reached.
files.page.upload_refusal_readonly: You have read access to this organization, so uploading is off.
files.page.upload_refusal_static_site: This is a static site's releases tree. Its files come from the last build, and anything written here would be replaced by the next deployment.
files.page.error_title: These files cannot be listed right now
files.page.read_only_note: This tree is read-only for you, so the operations that would change it are switched off.
files.page.show_dotfiles_hint: Hidden by default: what a customer came to see is their own files, and this is one tap.
files.page.folder_dropped_error: {names} {verb} a folder. Compress it first, upload the archive, then use Extract on it - that keeps the structure and survives a dropped connection, which a folder of loose files would not.
files.page.folder_empty_notice: That folder is empty, so there was nothing to upload.
files.page.folder_read_error: The browser would not read that folder. Try compressing it and uploading the archive instead.
files.page.folder_upload_hint: You can also drop a folder, or pick one below - its structure is reconstructed on the server.
files.page.load_more_error: The rest of this folder did not arrive. The node may have gone away.
files.page.delete_confirm_body: Folders are deleted with everything inside them. Nothing here goes to a bin.
files.page.symlink_notice: {name} is a link. The panel reports links and never follows them, so open what it points at directly.
files.page.too_large_notice: {name} is too large to open here. Downloading it instead.
files.list.empty_desc_all: Nothing here at all, including dotfiles. Upload something, or create a folder to put it in.
files.list.empty_desc_hidden: Nothing here, though dotfiles are hidden - turn them on if you are looking for one. Otherwise, upload a file or create a folder.
files.list.load_error_title: The rest of this folder did not arrive
files.list.sorted_note: · sorted within what has loaded so far
files.table.caption: Files in this folder
files.path.up_button_top: This is the top of the tree.
files.editor.revert_title_dirty: Put the file back to what was read
files.editor.save_title_readonly: This file is open for reading only.
files.editor.truncated_banner: This file is larger than the panel will open, so you are looking at the beginning of it. Saving is off: writing this buffer back would replace the whole file with the part that was read.
files.editor.binary_banner: This does not decode as text, so it is shown as far as it can be and saving is off - writing it back would replace every byte the decoder could not represent. Download it if you need the real contents.
files.editor.readonly_banner: This tree is read-only for you, so the file opens for reading. A static site's files come from its last build, and an edit here would be replaced by the next deployment.
files.editor.error_title: The file could not be opened
files.editor.loading_text: Reading the file from the node.
files.editor.default_read_error: The file could not be read. The node holding it may be unreachable.
files.editor.leave_confirm: This file has changes that have not been saved. Leave anyway?
files.editor.discard_confirm_body: The changes in this file have not been written to the volume.
files.upload.drop_or_pick: Drop files anywhere on the page, or pick them here.
files.upload.chunked_notice: Uploads are sent in chunks and carry on by themselves after a dropped connection - they resume from where they stopped rather than starting again.
files.upload.resumed_note: · carried on from where it stopped
files.drop.ready_desc: They go into {destination}, and carry on by themselves if the connection drops.
files.move.same_folder_error: That is the folder they are already in.
files.move.nothing_moved_error: Nothing was moved. The message above says what the panel refused.
files.move.partial_moved_error: {moved} of {count} moved. The rest were refused - the message above says why.
files.move.into_hint: Relative to the top of this tree. The folder has to exist already.
files.move.replace_hint: Off by default, so a move cannot quietly overwrite a file of the same name.
files.move.keeping_names: {count} entries, keeping the names they have now.
files.rename.title: Rename
files.rename.slash_error: A name cannot contain a slash. Use Move to put it in another folder.
files.rename.same_name_error: That is what it is already called.
files.rename.name_hint: Just the name. Renaming keeps it in this folder.
files.rename.overwrite_hint: Off by default. With this on, a file at the new name is overwritten and not recoverable.
files.new_folder.title: New folder
files.new_folder.description: It is created inside the folder you are looking at.
files.new_folder.name_hint: Letters, digits, dots, dashes. No slashes - this makes one folder.
files.permissions.title: Permissions
files.permissions.invalid_mode_error: Three or four octal digits, like 755.
files.permissions.mode_hint: Only owner, group and other read/write/execute are applied. setuid, setgid and the sticky bit are dropped.
files.permissions.recursive_hint: The node keeps directories enterable, so a recursive 644 does not lock you out of the tree.
files.measure.title: Folder size
files.measure.default_error: The node did not finish measuring this folder.
files.measure.walking: Walking the tree. A folder with a lot in it takes a few seconds.
files.measure.approximate_note: The node stopped at its walk budget, so the real total is larger than this. Measuring a smaller folder gives an exact answer.
files.archive.description: The node builds the archive; nothing is uploaded or downloaded to do it.
files.archive.path_hint: Relative to the top of this tree.
files.archive.summary_many: {count} entries from this folder, packed as they are named here.
files.extract.title: Unzip
files.extract.into_hint: Relative to the top of this tree. Leave it as it is to unpack here.
files.extract.overwrite_label: Replace files that are already there
files.extract.overwrite_hint: Off by default, so an archive cannot quietly overwrite work that is not in it.
terminal.page.not_placed_title: Nothing is running this service yet
terminal.page.not_placed_desc: A shell runs inside the container, so there has to be one. Start {name} and this page will open a shell in it - the platform places it on a node, pulls the image and reports back, which usually takes a few seconds.
terminal.page.readonly_title: You have read access to this organization
terminal.page.readonly_desc: A shell inside a container can do anything the application can, so opening one counts as changing things. Somebody with a developer role or above can open it, and logs and metrics are still available to you.
terminal.page.header_desc: /bin/sh inside the container. It ends by itself after {idle} idle, and after {max} whatever happens.
terminal.page.reconnecting_banner: The connection to the shell dropped and is being re-established. Anything typed in the meantime is held and sent when it comes back.
terminal.page.exit_banner: The shell ended with exit code {code}{reason}. Nothing in the container was stopped - only the shell.
terminal.page.no_shell_running: No shell is running. Opening this page does not start one - a terminal left open in a background tab is a process inside your container, so it is always something you ask for.
terminal.paste_dialog.title: Paste into the shell
terminal.paste_dialog.description: Your browser did not give the panel access to the clipboard, so paste it here instead.
terminal.paste_dialog.text_hint: Sent to the shell exactly as it is, including the line breaks.
files.new_file.title: New file
files.new_file.description: Create an empty file in this folder.
files.page.no_storage_desc: This service has no storage volumes mounted. Attach a volume in Storage settings to explore and manage files.
terminal.page.detached_banner: A previous shell session is still active (container {id}). You can resume your session without losing background processes.
files.page.quick_init_desc: Create a default 5 GiB data volume mounted at /app so you can upload files and code immediately.
